short: The treaty ending the Torstensson War, permanently shifting Baltic dominance to Sweden.
full:
Signed on 13 August 1645 after French mediation, the Treaty of Brömsebro concluded the brief but decisive Torstensson War between Sweden and Denmark-Norway. The terms were severely advantageous to Sweden, demanding the immediate cession of the Norwegian provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen, along with the Baltic islands of Gotland and Saaremaa. Furthermore, Sweden was granted exemption from the Sound Dues.

To guarantee the terms, Sweden occupied the Danish province of Halland for thirty years. This territorial realignment shattered the longstanding Danish hegemony in the region and secured Swedish supply lines to its armies in Germany. It marked the definitive tipping point in the Scandinavian balance of power, solidifying the Swedish Empire as the undisputed hegemon of the Baltic Sea.
